chat-message.context.ts: {density}. Provided by tct-chat-message-list, consumed here.

differences.text: `name` is an attribute and a slot; `avatar`, `metadata` and the body are slots. The article's accessible name is computed as text (the sender name, else "Message from {sender}") and set through ElementInternals, because upstream's aria-labelledby to the name element cannot cross the shadow root. `accessibleName` is a read-only getter the message list uses to introduce an announced message.

The avatar offset (one name row down, to line up with the first bubble's text) is driven by the bubble reporting its name row through chatMessageContext.reportName, where upstream uses `:has(~ * [data-chat-name])` across the flat DOM, which does not see through shadow roots.

A system message is named "Message from system" and shows no name row, as upstream; the element itself never re-renders for body changes (a streaming body): only the name slot's own subtree is observed, so 200 chunks cost the message nothing.

core.chat-message.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessible-web-components] (role and name through ElementInternals; ARIA relations stay inside one tree); [mwg:shadow-dom] (slots, whitespace); [mwg:css-layout] (logical flex layout, RTL for free).

differences.text: Upstream renders a fragment (name row, bubble, metadata row) into the message's flex column. The element is one host that fills the message column (`inline-size: 100%`) and lines the three rows up by sender inside it, so the bubble's `max(80%, 280px)` cap resolves against the column exactly as upstream's flat items do. Name and metadata rows appear only when there is something to show (non-rendering scalar values map to an absent attribute or empty slot).

The bubble content box is `display: flow-root`, not a flex column: a flex column makes every text run and inline element (<strong>, links) its own item, which splits a sentence into stacked lines. Block content (a card, an attachment list) stacks and stretches as it did.

Filled bubbles are --color-neutral for both senders (upstream's default; the React theme adds no chat-message-bubble override) with --radius-chat (Tecton radius.150, 12px) and --radius-container when compact. A transparent 1px outline draws the bubble's edge in forced colours.

core.chat-message-bubble.notes: Guides: [mwg:css-layout] (logical corner radii follow the reading direction); [mwg:styling-web-components] (private custom properties, parts).

differences.text: The status is an image (role=img) with the accessible name "Message {status}" and a native title with the status word. Upstream puts aria-label on a plain <span>, which has no role and so no supported name. The dots between the items are aria-hidden, where upstream leaves them in the reading order.
A failed status is drawn in --color-text-red (ink), not --color-error (the filled severity colour), to keep 4.5:1 on the page (React theme note for ChatToolCalls applies to every error ink).
Upstream returns null when there is nothing to show. The element renders nothing and is `display: contents`, so it takes no space and no flex gap in its parent.

core.chat-message-metadata.notes: Guides: [mwg:accessible-web-components] (status is an image with a name; separators are decorative); [mwg:css] (pulse only inside prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference).

api.notes: The message text is the `text` attribute, else the element's own text content (observed, so a stream can append to it). Only its text is read: markup inside it is shown as characters.
Property only. ChatToken = {value, label?, variant?, icon?} | {value, render}. `icon` is a registered icon name; `render` returns TemplateResult | Node | string (a string is text).

api.reason: A-xstyle: use class/style, ::part(base|token) or the tokens.

differences.text: The token types (ChatToken, ChatTokenBadge, ChatTokenCustom) live in chat-message.types.ts and are structurally upstream's ChatComposerToken. The composer (WP-16) imports them from here, so one definition serves input and display.

No HTML-string sink: the text, token labels and any string a custom renderer returns are Lit text bindings, never markup. `announcementText` exposes the text as displayed (a mention by its label) so the message list announces what the reader sees.

Known open item (not this folder's): in the dark theme the orange, pink and yellow hue badges fall under 4.5:1 when they sit on a chat bubble (--color-neutral), because the hue fills are tinted over the surface. Every hue passes on the page background and in light mode. Badge tokens belong to WP-2/tokens; the docs example uses the blue, green and purple variants.

core.chat-tokenized-text.notes: Guides: [mwg:trusted-types] (no HTML sinks; Lit templates only); [mwg:shadow-dom] (unassigned light-DOM text is not rendered, so it is the source and never shown twice).
